target.title: fix(security): add estimate-before-decode guard to base64 paths
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large base64-encoded images can cause transient memory pressure during decoding. This PR adds a size estimation check before decoding base64 image data in CLI staging, provider image-parsing paths, and the Codex/OpenAI OAuth image-generation result route, and propagates the existing configured media size limit through these new guards.

**Security impact**: Defense-in-depth against transient memory exhaustion from oversized base64 payloads.

## Summary

- Reuses the existing public `estimateBase64DecodedBytes` helper (`@openclaw/media-core/base64`) to estimate decoded byte length before decoding
- Propagates existing `maxBytes` limit through:
  - CLI image writing (`writeCliImages`, in `src/agents/cli-runner/cli-images.ts`)
  - Provider image parsing (`generatedImageAssetFromBase64`)
  - **Codex/OpenAI OAuth image-generation result route** (`parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse` threads `maxBytes`)
- Boundary tests for configured-limit acceptance, over-limit rejection before decode, default-limit enforcement, and Codex OAuth route oversized-entry drop
- **No new configuration**: uses the existing `generatedMediaMaxBytes` setting
- **No new public package API**: the CLI staging guard is a private function in `cli-images.ts` built on the existing `estimateBase64DecodedBytes` export (per review feedback, the earlier `@openclaw/media-core/base64-size-limit` subpath was removed)

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof (final head, 2026-07-19)

Both guarded base64 paths were executed directly on the exact PR head via `tsx` (no mocks — real function calls through the public entry `prepareCliPromptImagePayload`, real filesystem staging):

```bash
./node_modules/.bin/tsx runtime-proof.mts
```

```text
date: Sun Jul 19 2026 08:11:59 GMT+0800 (中国标准时间)
node: v24.18.0
default MAX_IMAGE_BYTES=6291456
code path: cli-images.ts prepareCliPromptImagePayload + image-assets.ts @ PR head
[cli staging valid] accepted: imagePaths=1 file=/tmp/openclaw/openclaw-cli-images/6a2b0d3f….png
[cli staging over-limit] rejected before decode: Base64 payload exceeds size limit: 6295552 bytes > 6291456 bytes
[provider parser valid] accepted: assets=1 mime=image/png bytes=70
[provider parser over-limit] rejected before decode: assets=0 (expect 0)
```

- **CLI staging (`prepareCliPromptImagePayload` → private `writeCliImages` guard)**: a valid 1×1 PNG is staged to a private file; a payload 4 KB over the 6 MiB default budget is rejected by the estimate-before-decode guard with a clear size error — `Buffer.from(data, "base64")` is never reached for the over-limit input.
- **Provider parser (`parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse`)**: a valid `b64_json` entry under the budget produces one asset (70 decoded bytes, sniffed `image/png`); the over-limit payload is dropped before decode (`assets=0`).

## Regression tests (final head)

```bash
pnpm vitest run src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts src/image-generation/image-assets.test.ts \
  src/music-generation/provider-assets.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner.spawn.test.ts \
  src/agents/cli-runner/claude-live-session.background-tasks.test.ts src/agents/utils/image-resize.test.ts
```

```text
Test Files  10 passed (10)
     Tests  304 passed (304)
```

(Private helpers are exercised through `cli-images.test-support.ts`, the repo's globalThis test-api pattern; `writeCliSystemPromptFile` is imported from `cli-images.js` directly.)

## What was not tested

- Live provider OOM reproduction (neither necessary nor safely desirable). The proof above exercises the exact guard branches on the final head.

## CI note

Earlier-head failures traced to this branch, not main: a stale `../../sandbox/fs-bridge.js` import path, the moved `writeCliSystemPromptFile` no longer exported from `helpers.ts`, knip unused-export findings (test-only consumers), and unrelated `image-resize.ts` churn. Current head: helpers stay private with test access via `cli-images.test-support.ts`, tests import from `cli-images.js` directly, `image-resize.ts` matches main, and oxlint/knip/tsgo all pass locally. Branch is rebased onto latest main.

## Compatibility conclusion — Codex OAuth image-response route (review P2)

Inspected the exact sibling contract in `extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.ts`: main already caps the HTTP JSON payload via `readProviderJsonResponse(maxBytes: count × per-image budget)` but decodes **every** base64 entry without a per-image budget; the PR head passes `maxBytes: resolveGeneratedImageMaxBytes(cfg)` into `parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse`. Runtime contract check on the final head:

```text
date: Sun Jul 19 2026 12:18:44 GMT+0800 (中国标准时间)
route contract: parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse(data, { maxBytes: resolveGeneratedImageMaxBytes(cfg) })
[mixed payload] in=2 entries -> out=1 asset(s) (oversized dropped, valid kept)
[single oversized] out=0 assets -> provider throws "OpenAI image generation response missing image data"
[prior contract, no maxBytes] out=1 asset(s), bytes=6295552 (would previously decode)
```

**Conclusion:** the only observable compatibility delta is for individual images exceeding the per-image budget (default 6 MiB, or configured `mediaMaxMb`) — previously decoded (up to the HTTP-level aggregate cap), now dropped before decode; a fully-oversized response now fails closed with the provider's existing "missing image data" error instead of materializing an over-budget image. Mixed responses keep all in-budget images. This is the intended security behavior of the PR; no other runtime contract changes.
